subquestion: Q1: determine whether each supplied microstructure conducts from the left charged face to the right charged face and return an auditable conductor path
target_claim: For each of the three official coordinate groups, classify left-to-right connectivity under the stated 1.8 nm surface-gap rule and exhibit a valid node chain whenever connected.

data_audit.missingness_notes: No missing coordinates; truncated boundary segments must remain truncated rather than being extended to 5000 nm.

baseline.name: endpoint-and-center proximity graph
baseline.reason: A transparent lower-effort comparator reveals errors caused by replacing segment distance with point distance.
baseline.implementation: Connect rods when endpoint or center distances fall below 61.8 nm; add virtual left/right face nodes.
baseline.validation: Compare classifications and edges with the exact geometry model; disagreement is expected evidence against the baseline.

candidates.name: analytic capsule graph with periodic images and union-find
candidates.formulation: Represent each supplied rod by its observed axis segment. Compute exact segment-to-segment minimum distance over the finite set of relevant periodic image translations, connect pairs at distance <=61.8 nm, connect face-touching rods to virtual electrodes, then use union-find and BFS parent recovery.
assumptions: The supplied endpoints define the conductive axis actually present in the cube.
Periodic wrapping follows the official boundary rule.
A surface gap <=1.8 nm is conductive.
validation_plan: unit-test intersecting, parallel, skew, tangent and degenerate segments
recompute every selected path edge independently
compare all near-threshold pairs with the fallback solver
refutation_evidence: any returned path edge exceeds 61.8 nm after independent recomputation
classification changes under algebraically equivalent endpoint ordering
periodic translation search misses a brute-force image case
expected_failure_modes: false face contact from radius/axis confusion
candidates.decision_reason: It is exact for finite line segments, computationally trivial at 535 rods, and returns an auditable path rather than only a label.

candidates.name: independent bounded segment-distance minimization
candidates.formulation: For every candidate rod pair and periodic image, minimize squared Euclidean distance over segment parameters (s,t) in [0,1]^2 using an independently implemented bounded quadratic solver, then build the same graph.
assumptions: The same finite-segment and periodic-boundary interpretation as the primary model.
validation_plan: cross-check near-threshold distances against the analytic implementation
verify KKT/bound constraints and objective values
refutation_evidence: solver returns an out-of-bounds segment parameter
objective differs materially from brute-force dense samples on stress cases
expected_failure_modes: optimizer tolerance masks a threshold edge
candidates.decision_reason: It is algorithmically independent enough to diagnose analytic edge-case errors while remaining tractable.

candidates.name: whole-cube voxel percolation
candidates.formulation: Rasterize the 10000 nm cube and test connected occupied voxels.
assumptions: A finite voxel width preserves 1.8 nm gaps.
validation_plan: compare several voxel widths against exact tangent cases
rejection_evidence: Resolving a 1.8 nm gap in a 10000 nm cube would require an impractical grid and still introduces orientation aliasing.
candidates.decision_reason: It adds discretization bias and extreme cost where exact finite-segment geometry is available.

primary_model: analytic capsule graph with periodic images and union-find
stop_conditions: official periodic-boundary wording cannot be reconciled with the supplied coordinates
primary and fallback disagree on any edge more than numerical tolerance permits
an explicit conducting path cannot be reconstructed for a positive classification
